targetText: Bismarck granted in numbers just sufficient to keep the civil war a-going, and keep the Versailles government in abject dependence on Prussia
summary: Prussian collusion with Versailles: Bismarck released captured French troops to allow Thiers to crush the Paris Commune.
explanation: Marx exposes the counter-revolutionary collusion between Prussian militarism and French capitalists: Bismarck released captured French soldiers to bolster Thiers's army against Parisian workers.

targetText: bourgeoisie of the whole world, which looks complacently upon the wholesale massacre after the battle, is convulsed by horror at the desecration of brick and mortar
summary: Bourgeois hypocrisy: prioritizing private property and buildings over human working-class lives.
explanation: Marx exposes how the international capitalist class ignored the bloody slaughter of 30,000 workers while hypocritically weeping over damaged buildings during the Communard defense.

targetText: real murderer of Archbishop Darboy is Thiers. The Commune again and again had offered to exchange the archbishop, and ever so many priests in the bargain, against the single Blanqui, then in the hands of Thiers. Thiers obstinately refused
summary: The hostage exchange refusal: Thiers deliberately sacrificed the Archbishop to justify the wholesale murder of Communards.
explanation: The Commune repeatedly offered to trade Archbishop Darboy for Auguste Blanqui, but Thiers refused because he wanted the Archbishop killed to smear the Commune as ruthless murderers.

targetText: conquering and the conquered hosts should fraternize for the common massacre of the proletariat
summary: International class solidarity of capital: enemy armies uniting to crush working-class revolution.
explanation: Marx highlights the ultimate proof of class rule: French and Prussian armies set aside their national war to collaborate in slaughtering the Parisian working class.

targetText: Class rule is no longer able to disguise itself in a national uniform; the national governments are one as against the proletariat
summary: Nationalism exposed as bourgeois humbug: capitalist state apparatuses form an international alliance against the working class.
explanation: Marx concludes that national wars are mere ruling-class diversions. When working-class revolution threatens capital, all national governments unite as one force against the proletariat.

targetText: Working men's Paris, with its Commune, will be forever celebrated as the glorious harbinger of a new society
summary: Immortal legacy of the Paris Commune: Paris Communards enshrined as pioneers of a future socialist world.
explanation: Marx immortalizes the heroic struggle of the Paris Commune, asserting that its lessons and martyrs will forever inspire the global working-class movement for social emancipation.
